subtopic: Prometheus Metrics Types (Counter, Gauge, Histogram, Summary)
question_text: [Observability, Telemetry & Incident Mitigation - Q10] Why is a Prometheus `Counter` metric reset-resilient when queried using the `rate()` function in PromQL?

options.text: Prometheus stores counter values in Redis
The `rate()` function automatically detects when counter values drop (indicating process restart) and adjusts calculations to handle counter resets seamlessly
Counters cannot be reset in Linux
Rate function only works on Gauges

answer_explanation: The `rate()` and `irate()` functions in PromQL assume counters strictly increase, so any observed decrease is interpreted as an instance restart, adding the counter value before reset.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: The `rate()` and `irate()` functions in PromQL assume counters strictly increase, so any observed decrease is interpreted as an instance restart, adding the counter value before reset.
